I'll think through this as Wang — a middle-school-educated woman farming 2.6 mu in Quzhou.

---

My land is only 2.6 mu, so I cannot waste money, but I also cannot let the harvest be bad — four mouths depend on this plot and what my husband sends home. I do wheat-maize rotation like everyone in our village. Last year my wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu and maize about 550 kg per mu, so I will follow the same way and adjust a little.

**Wheat (October to June):** I already planted winter wheat last autumn. For the base fertilizer I put down about 2 bags of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu before ploughing — that is 50 kg, so roughly 7.5 kg N, 7.5 kg P, 7.5 kg K per mu. In spring at green-up and jointing I will topdress urea, maybe 20 kg per mu total, that adds another 9 kg of N. So all together around 16-17 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K. The dealer told me I could use less but my neighbor cut back two years ago and her wheat looked yellow, so I keep my amount. I will irrigate at green-up, jointing, and grain-filling — three times with the well. Spray once for aphids and red spider, once for wheat scab when it heads. I use rotary tillage because that is what the tractor service does for us.

**Summer maize (June to October):** After wheat harvest I plant Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid — improved seed, everyone uses it. I do no-tillage direct seeding right into the wheat stubble, it saves the tractor fee. Base I put a half bag compound per mu (about 12 kg), then topdress urea 25 kg at big-bell stage — that gives roughly 15 kg N, 2 kg P, 2 kg K. Maize is hungry for nitrogen, so the urea matters most. I irrigate twice — once after sowing if no rain, once at tasseling. Spray for corn borer once, maybe a herbicide at seedling stage, so two sprays.

I keep costs around 300-350 yuan per mu on fertilizer and 60-80 on pesticide. Anything I save goes to the children.
